newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr at two-yr high on mark after German data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr at two-yr high on mark after German data.

text.p: The dollar rose to a two-year high against the mark on Thursday after a weak set of German data and it firmed on the yen following another plunge in Tokyo stocks sparked by worries over huge Japanese bank debts.
The three percent share tumble in Tokyo overnight plus a 51-point drop in Wall Street did nothing to calm nerves on European bourses, where there was increased anxiety about interest rates.
London, Frankfurt and Paris were all lower in morning trading, though the Paris exchange was supported by merger rumours.

The dollar's rise to its new two-year high just above 1.58 marks came after Germany announced a jobless hike to a seasonally adjusted 4.156 million in December, a new post-war record and after figures showing the German economy grew provisionally at a real 1.4 percent rate in 1996, marginally slower than economists had expected.
The data prompted speculation that German rates would be trimmed again at some stage but analysts said no cut was expected at Thursday's regular meeting of the Bundesbank council.

Another factor tending to boost the dollar over the mark was concern over the health of Russian president Boris Yeltsin, who has been admitted to hospital with pneumonia. Any threat of instability in Russia tends to have a negative effect on the German currency.

The continuing freefall in Tokyo stocks, sparked by worries that the nation's major banks cannot solve their huge debt problems and broader concerns about the health of the Japanese economy, weakened the yen. In morning European trading the dollar was quoted at 116.25 yen, up from 115.90 late in Europe on Wednesday.

On the equity front, leading London shares were down almost three quarters of a percent by 1000 GMT and dealers said the falls in Tokyo and Wall Street as well interest rate worries were damaging sentiment.

Rising U.S. bond yields have spooked investors on both sides of the Atlantic, prompting speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve may increase its short-term funds rate as early as next month, they said.
"With the U.S. long bond yield pushing closer to seven percent, the market is getting more and more nervous about a rate hike," one dealer commented.
Key U.S. producer price data (expected at 1330 GMT) was the main focus of market attention on Thursday ahead of the Dow's 1430 GMT start.
A Reuters poll of economists forecast the U.S. producer pricess, an important clue to future credit policy, to rise by 0.3 percent in December compared with a 0.4 percent increase the previous month.

In Frankfurt German shares were little moved by the German unemployment data but dealers said the the overnight weakness on Wall Street was holding the market down. The blue chip DAX index was down over half a percent by 1000 GMT.
It was a similar story in Paris, where dealers cited the Tokyo tumble and the Dow's 50-point drop for soft prices.
However, Societe Generale's planned purchase of Credit du Nord from Paribas kept merger interest alive and rumours were circulating over another big, unidentified, acquisition.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.58 marks and 116.25 yen compared with 1.5758 marks and 115.90 yen late in Europe on Wednesday. STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was down 27.3 at 4060.2, the Frankfurt DAX index was down 17.15 points at 2889.19 and the Paris CAC-40 index was down 1.07 2330.52.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was quoted at $354.25 compared with its London close of $355.75 on Wednesday. Silver was unchanged at $4.66.
